properties.name: Berkshire Botanical Garden
properties.planningFocus: Multi-scale public-garden, bed, and infrastructure planning
properties.summary: A four-parcel campus interpretation with all 33 numbered visitor-map landmarks, 47 regularized bed-grid cell estimates, one separate Discovery Garden planning bed, and connected circulation modeled independently from beds.

mapping.method: The complete public campus was matched to four adjacent MassGIS Level 3 parcel records totaling 23.86 acres. The official visitor map supplies the 1–33 landmark vocabulary and schematic relationships, while MassGIS orthophotos support independent interior interpretation. The 47 bed cells are a regularized grid inferred from six retained raster center controls; their dimensions, rotations, and polygon edges are not individually traced or surveyed. One planning-only Discovery Garden bed remains separate, and paths and drives are connected infrastructure rather than bed-like rectangles.

layoutCalibration.target: Full 33-landmark campus with 35 Edible Gardens and 12 Children's Vegetable Garden regularized bed-grid cells, one separate Discovery Garden planning bed, and continuous road, path, and trail networks
layoutCalibration.reference: Berkshire Botanical Garden 2024 self-guided visitor map
layoutCalibration.note: The 35-cell Edible Gardens grid and 12-cell Children's Vegetable Garden grid are regularized estimates. Six cell centers have explicit raster controls; the other centers are interpolated, and all cell boundaries use generalized dimensions and rotation. Crop taxa are not claimed as observations. The Discovery food-and-flower bed is a low-confidence planning proposal. Roads, paths, and trails are connected LineString centerlines in an infrastructure edit collection distinct from beds. Every interior feature remains non-surveyed.

gridEstimateGroups.geometryBasis: Regular-grid interpolation from four retained Edible Gardens center controls; generalized cell dimensions and rotation
Regular-grid interpolation from two retained Children's Garden center controls; generalized cell dimensions and rotation

infrastructure.geometryModel: Connected LineString centerlines with shared endpoint and topology-node identifiers

provenance.evidenceBoundary: The visitor map supplies names, numbers, and schematic relationships; orthophotos supply editable metric geometry; planned study beds and planting assignments are proposals rather than observations. The user-supplied KMZ is an opt-in comparison layer and contributes zero canonical features.

referenceMapPresentation.note: The illustrated visitor map is rotated. A browser bearing near +30 to +33 degrees can aid comparison, but canonical local and CRS84 geometry remains north-up.

layoutAnchor.method: Aerial-calibrated local origin for the editable BBG interpretation; interior features remain non-surveyed.

properties.name: The Mount · formal gardens
properties.summary: Manually reconstructed site features from 2025 aerial imagery, cross-referenced with publisher maps. Canopy-obscured boundaries remain uncertain; planting-bed design is deferred.

mapping.method: The official published location was matched to MassGIS Level 3 parcel 1_5_0. The editable origin is registered to the rectangular former kitchen-garden lawn immediately north of the stable using The Mount's garden documentation, the 2018 SculptureNow estate map, and MassGIS 2025 aerial imagery; the kitchen-bed geometry remains diagrammatic.

layoutCalibration.reference: The Mount garden documentation and 2018 SculptureNow estate map
layoutCalibration.note: Source pixel picks retained per feature. Garden boundaries obscured by canopy remain low confidence; planting design is deferred.

layoutAnchor.method: Historical local coordinate origin retained for saved-workspace compatibility; the reviewed site viewport and geographic feature geometry determine display.
